newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-O/N RATES FALL SHARPLY, LAT EASES AGAINST DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-O/N RATES FALL SHARPLY, LAT EASES AGAINST DOLLAR.

text.p: Overnight rates maintained their sharp fall on Wednesday as banks fulfilled their liquidity requirements and the lat eased against the dollar, dealers said.
Overnight rates fell to a bid/ask 1.50/2.25 percent on Wednesday from 3.00/3.50 percent on Tuesday and dealers said they could fall further.
"It is the end of the month, and most banks have fulfilled their obligatory reserve requirements," said Maris Vinklers, head of money markets at Hansabank-Latvija.
"They could even fall to 0.5/1.50 percent," he said.
On the foreign exchange markets, the lat eased slightly against the strengthening dollar, which gained against the Japanese yen and other currencies in the SDR basket which the lat is pegged to.
The interbank rate was trading in a very narrow range of 0.5842/5844, near the central bank intervention rate of 0.5837.
Dealers said the market was quiet and last week's demand for lats ahead of Monday's auction of one million of the state's shares in Unibanka had tapered off.
